_purpose: T106 fixture (SpecKit-004 'fast-dev-cycles', User Story 4 / Phase E, plan.md T-E03, tasks.md T106). Defines the CORE / governance-SUBSET / PER-ITEM text blocks for two consecutive same-CLASS dispatches, consumed ONLY by this test's own independent derive_prompt() oracle (constitution 11.4.245) below -- NEVER by context/dispatch_prefix.py (T115, does not exist yet). 'Same class' here means: dispatch 1 and dispatch 2 were computed T-E01's governance_subset selection to the SAME anchor set for the SAME core -- i.e. core_text and subset_text_class_a are IDENTICAL bytes across both dispatches; only each dispatch's own per_item text (which embeds a fresh timestamp) differs. Not real dispatch content; every string below is a fixture literal.
core_text: FASTCYCLE fixture (T106) CORE preamble block. This text is identical, byte-for-byte, across every dispatch regardless of class -- the always-loaded root per T-E01/T-E02's own core/on-demand split. It never varies with the item, the class, or the timestamp.
subset_text_class_a: FASTCYCLE fixture (T106) governance SUBSET block for dispatch class FC-PFX-A. This text is identical, byte-for-byte, across every dispatch classified as FC-PFX-A by T-E01's governance_subset selector -- it varies ONLY when the item's classification (and therefore its selected anchor set) differs, never with the timestamp or the per-item body.
dispatch_1_per_item: 2026-09-29T22:01:07+05:00 item=? T106 fixture dispatch 1 of 2 (class FC-PFX-A): investigate the first half of the scenario. Not a real dispatch.
dispatch_2_per_item: 2026-09-29T22:04:33+05:00 item=? T106 fixture dispatch 2 of 2 (class FC-PFX-A, SAME class as dispatch 1): investigate the second half of the scenario. Not a real dispatch.
_note_on_the_bound_used_by_the_test: dispatch_1_per_item and dispatch_2_per_item share a short leading substring (their common ISO-timestamp date/hour prefix, '2026-09-29T22:0') before diverging -- so the broken-order shared-prefix length is NOT necessarily exactly 0. This test therefore does NOT assert an exact-zero broken-order length (that would be a brittle, fixture-wording-dependent claim); it asserts the general, provably-true bound instead: correct_shared_len >= len(core_text)+len(subset_text_class_a) (core+subset are byte-identical across both dispatches by construction, so they are ALWAYS a common prefix when placed first) and broken_shared_len < len(dispatch_1_per_item) (the common prefix of (P1+CS, P2+CS) for P1 != P2 can never exceed min(len(P1),len(P2)) -- it can never cross into the trailing core+subset bytes at all once P1 and P2 diverge, which they do well before either string ends). Both bounds hold regardless of exactly how much P1/P2 happen to share at the start, and correct_shared_len > broken_shared_len follows directly since len(core_text)+len(subset_text_class_a) is, by design, far larger than len(dispatch_1_per_item).
